correctness.rationale: Exact Haar left-nullspace normal on the rank-r support yields a rank-one PSD residual whose trace is an inverse spherical quadratic form. Haar last-coordinate density and bounded positive anisotropic q(u) give dominated-convergence subcritical moments, logarithmic critical integration, and integrable t/sqrt(eps) scaling above order 1/2. Direct conditional threshold inversion proves the rare-error coefficient. The planar mean follows from an angular Cauchy integral. A standalone script passed 140 matrix identities, 16 exact planar integrals, four rank-dependent constants, tested moment orders and anisotropic and rare-event checks. The analytic proof, not finite tests, establishes generality.

value.rationale: Zero oversampling is the mathematically natural boundary excluded by common Nyström expected-error theorems. For exactly one weak eigenvalue, typical error is order ε while mean error is order sqrt(ε), and the ratio to optimal error diverges; the exact half-moment phase transition, anisotropic leading constants and √ε probability coefficient explain the nontrivial rare-event mechanism across every fixed rank.
